title: Canary Telemetry Workbench — Lab Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab notebook for a lightweight telemetry workbench to support cross-functional canary and A/B rollouts. The goal is to make signal design, simulation, and change review fast for Product, SRE, and Engineering so we can iterate on releases without over-indexing on false positives.

Scope & intended users:
- Primary: product owners running canary/A-B experiments, rollout stewards, SRE oncall.
- Secondary: solutions engineering (customer-facing canaries), privacy/security reviewers for private deployments.
- Not in scope: replacing full observability platform or audit logs. This is a fast-feedback layer that sits on top of metrics/logs/traces.

High-level idea (simple):
- Define a small set of telemetry "primitives" that every rollout uses (latency, p50/p95, error-rate, hallucination-rate proxy, cost-per-request, saturation signals).
- Provide a one-click simulator that replays historical traffic slices to surface how signals behave and whether thresholds would have fired.
- Keep an audit-friendly review flow (git-like diffs) for telemetry changes so PM/Eng/SRE can approve new triggers.

Telemetry primitives (first pass):
- request.latency.ms.p50 (rolling 5m)
- request.latency.ms.p95 (rolling 5m)
- request.errors.count (5m) and request.errors.rate (5m)
- model.response.unexpected_tokens.rate (proxy for hallucination; uses evaluator probes or heuristics)
- cost.cpu.gpu.token (estimated cost per token)
- kvcache.miss.rate (important for long-session workloads)
- queue.length / queue.latency (backpressure)
- user-visible-failure.rate (end-to-end customer impact)

Default signal families and examples:
- Latency family: p95 > baseline * 1.8 for 5m -> SEV page; p95 > baseline * 1.5 for 10m -> paging to oncall.
- Error family: absolute errors > X/min OR increase > 3x baseline -> immediate traffic hold.
- Quality family: hallucination-proxy > 1.2x baseline for 1h -> quarantined slice + manual review.
- Cost family: cost/token exceeds predicted by >20% for 30m -> steward notification (no automatic kill).

Simulator & replay workbench notes:
- Replay engine should run differential checks: compare canary candidate vs control slices across the same historical traces.
- Need lightweight synthetic probes (prompt templates) that exercise known failure modes (out-of-scope responses, rate-limiting errors, large-reply generator).
- Implement a "tolerability matrix" that lets PMs mark which signals can be tolerated for a short period (e.g., cost spike ok during business hours with human-in-loop).
- Save replay runs as artifacts: parameters, trace ids, diff snapshots, plots. These artifacts are attached to the rollout ticket.

Cross-functional responsibilities (proposal):
- Product: defines which user journeys the canary covers and tolerability preferences; owns experiment hypothesis and final go/no-go.
- Engineering: ships canary variant and integrates telemetry tags; owns synthetic probe definitions and metric instrumentation.
- SRE: defines alert-to-action mapping for primitives and enforces escalation. Builds the replay tooling and sim runner.
- Customer Success: provides customer-scope slices for staged rollouts when needed and interprets customer-surface signals.
- Security/Compliance: reviews telemetry artifacts for sensitive data or PII leakage in probes.

Review/approval flow (git-like):
- Change authored as telemetry proposal JSON diff (primitives, thresholds, dashboards).
- Auto-run simulator with new thresholds against last 30d of traffic and attach report.
- Stakeholder reviewers: product + eng + SRE must +1 before activation. Keep a 48h default review window for non-urgent changes.
- All activations create a rollout ticket with a link to the simulator run.

Signal prioritization heuristic (lab draft):
- Severity score = (user-impact weight * incidence) + (platform-impact weight * resource delta) + (stability weight * historical volatility).
- Weight table is tunable per-product; default assigns highest to user-visible failures, medium to latency, lower to cost.

Example runbook excerpts (quick):
- If request.errors.rate > 4% for 5m (and increase > 2x baseline) -> hold canary traffic to 0% and alert oncall.
- If p95 latency increases 1.6x but CPU/GPU utilization < 60% -> mark for routing investigation (suspect model behavior).
- If hallucination-proxy > threshold for microcohort (VIP users) -> immediate rollback for that cohort and manual review.

Dashboards and quick queries (templates):
- PromQL p95 template: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model_variant))
- Error-rate baseline: (sum(rate(errors_total[5m])) by (route, cohort)) / (sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (route, cohort))
- Diff view: compute per-minute percentage delta between canary and control for p95 and error-rate, visualize 95th percentile of deltas.

Experiment lifecycle timeline (example):
1) Draft telemetry proposal + simulator run attached (day -5 to -2)
2) Review window + PR fixes (day -2 to -1)
3) Deploy canary to 0.5% -> 5% ramp over 6 hours (with auto-checkpoints)
4) Monitor 1h/3h/24h signals; if green -> continue ramp to 25% then 100%
5) Rollback rules check at each checkpoint (automated and human gates)

Open questions / unresolved items (TODOs):
- How to instrument and compute a robust hallucination proxy across models (we have initial heuristics, but need better labelling pipelines).
- Ownership for maintaining the simulator's historical trace store (S3 vs HDFS vs internal trace-db).
- How to integrate privacy redaction for probe transcripts that may contain customer text.
- Do we allow product to toggle non-critical signals (cost) without SRE signoff? proposal: allow but notify SRE immediately.

Immediate next actions (short-term sprint):
- Samir: prototype replay diff UI + save artifacts (spike, 4d).
- Lina: write 6 synthetic probe templates and add to probe catalog (3d).
- Tomás: draft telemetry-change PR template and reviewer checklist (2d).
- Maya: consolidate tolerability matrix and run a tabletop with SRE/product on 2025-02-05.

Notes to self / friction points we've seen in previous rollouts:
- Too many low-quality alerts drown out signal. We need a default "signal hygiene" step for every telemetry change.
- Product teams often conflate short-term acceptable degradation (e.g., expensive but higher quality) with permanent thresholds. Make tolerability explicit.
- Simulator runtime must be fast (<30m for 7d traces) or people won't use it. Start small: 24–72h slices for quick iteration.

Closing: this doc is intentionally terse. The aim is to get an MVP in place for the next two canary runs (Jan–Feb). Feedback loop: drop comments in the linked Slack thread (see linked_artifacts) and add any additional probe ideas below.

Probe ideas (scratchpad):
- repeated-asking probe: asks same question twice with small context drift -> measures model consistency.
- safety-edge probe: prompts that flirt with policy boundaries to detect drift.
- memory-frag probe: long-session prompts that exercise KV cache eviction patterns.

-- end --
